name: The ten offences against the name
description: Blaspheming devotees; regarding Śiva's names and qualities as independent of Viṣṇu's; disregarding the guru; deriding scripture; taking the name's glories as exaggeration; interpreting the name fancifully; sinning on its strength; equating it with other pious acts; teaching it to the faithless; lacking love for it despite hearing its glories (clinging to 'I and mine'); inattention is often added.
members: no love despite hearing its glory

name: Offences in deity worship (sevāparādha)
description: Offences against the deity in worship — impurity, disrespect, improper conduct in the temple — listed in the Haribhaktivilāsa (from the Purāṇas); number and list to verify.

name: The four kinds of unwanted things (anartha)
description: Unwanted tendencies arising from past sins, from pious acts (desire for their fruits), from offences, and from devotion itself (desire for gain, honour, prestige); removed in the anartha-nivṛtti stage.
notes: A different fourfold list (svarūpa-bhrama, asat-tṛṣṇā, aparādha, hṛdaya-daurbalya) is given by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura (recent).

name: Six things that destroy devotion
description: Overeating or over-collecting, over-endeavour, idle talk, rigid attachment to (or neglect of) rules, worldly company, greed or fickleness.
antidotes: the six things that nourish devotion (Upadeśāmṛta 3)

name: Desire for enjoyment and liberation
description: The 'witch' of desire for worldly or heavenly enjoyment and for liberation, which prevents the joy of devotion; with desire for powers (siddhi) it makes one restless.

name: Desire for other than Kṛṣṇa (anyābhilāṣa)
description: Any desire other than for Kṛṣṇa's service, and devotion covered by the aims of knowledge (impersonal oneness) or works.

name: Desire for prestige (pratiṣṭhāśā)
description: The desire for fame and honour, 'a shameless outcaste woman dancing in the heart', the most persistent anartha, which keeps pure love out.

name: Lust (kāma) as counterfeit of love
description: Desire for one's own sense-pleasure, contrasted with prema, the desire for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure.

name: Semblance of devotional emotion (ratyābhāsa)
description: Apparent ecstasy or emotion — reflected or shadow-like — in those whose hearts are impure or whose aims are other; outward signs imitated without bhāva.

name: Sleepiness (laya)
description: Drowsiness or dullness during hearing, chanting and remembrance, an obstacle to steadiness (niṣṭhā).
notes: Partial parallel: Vedāntasāra's laya among the obstacles to samādhi (list of obstacles to nirvikalpa samādhi; U13). Viśvanātha adds apratipatti.

name: Distraction (vikṣepa)
description: The mind's wandering to worldly topics during practice.
notes: Partial parallel: Vedāntasāra's vikṣepa (list of obstacles to nirvikalpa samādhi; U13). Viśvanātha adds apratipatti.

name: Incapacity or indifference (apratipatti)
description: Inability or disinclination to engage in practice even when free of sleep and distraction.

name: Residual impurity (kaṣāya)
description: Latent tendencies (anger, greed, pride) that rise up and colour practice.
notes: Partial parallel: Vedāntasāra's kaṣāya (list of obstacles to nirvikalpa samādhi; U13). Viśvanātha adds apratipatti.

name: Relish of other pleasures (rasāsvāda)
description: The mind turning to taste worldly pleasures during practice.
notes: Partial parallel: Vedāntasāra's rasāsvāda (there: relishing the bliss of savikalpa samādhi) — same word, different object (list of obstacles to nirvikalpa samādhi; U13). Viśvanātha adds apratipatti.

name: The three obstacles to service (Sevāphala)
description: Agitation of mind (udvega), external hindrance (pratibandha) and attachment to enjoyment (bhoga), which impede the fruits of service.

name: The five kinds of faults removed by brahmasambandha
description: Innate faults, those arising from place and time, those determined by worldly and Vedic rule, those arising from association and those from contact.

name: Five-jointed ignorance (Vallabha)
description: Forgetting one's nature and identifying with body, senses, vital breath and inner organ.

name: Taking refuge in other than Kṛṣṇa (anyāśraya)
description: Seeking refuge in other gods, paths or worldly supports, which the Puṣṭimārga forbids to those who have taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa.

name: Bondage by real adjuncts (Bhāskara)
description: The soul's delimitation by real adjuncts (body, senses, intellect) due to beginningless karma and ignorance; they end only with the body.
